topics.title: The cell and cell processes
topics.concept: The cell is the basic unit of life. Plant and animal cells share most organelles but differ in a few structures; substances cross the cell membrane by passive and active transport.

subtopics.title: Plant and animal cell organelles
subtopics.concept: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall, plastids (chloroplasts) and a large central vacuole. The Grade 9 textbook lists centrioles and lysosomes as found only in animal cells. Ribosomes occur in all cells; eukaryotic cells have a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles, prokaryotes (bacteria) do not.

textbook_refs.section: 1.2.2 The Cell Structure – plant cell organelles

subtopics.title: Diffusion, osmosis and active transport
subtopics.concept: Diffusion and osmosis are passive (no energy, down a concentration gradient; osmosis = water through a selectively permeable membrane). Active transport moves molecules into or out of the cell with the help of energy (ATP), even against a concentration gradient.

topics.title: Bacteria, viruses and protists
topics.concept: Bacteria (Monera) are prokaryotes that reproduce by binary fission and sometimes conjugation; viruses are obligate intracellular parasites; protists include unicellular algae such as Euglena.

subtopics.title: Bacterial and viral diseases; bacterial reproduction
subtopics.concept: Bacterial diseases: gonorrhoea (Neisseria gonorrhoeae), syphilis (Treponema pallidum), tetanus, pneumonia, tuberculosis, salmonellosis, anthrax. Viral diseases: smallpox, common cold, chickenpox, influenza, herpes, polio, rabies, Ebola, HIV/AIDS. Some bacteria (E. coli) exchange genetic material by conjugation, a primitive sexual reproduction.

textbook_refs.section: 1.4.2 Economic Importance of Bacteria – animal diseases (salmonellosis)
1.4.2 The Economic Importance of Bacteria – human diseases

subtopics.title: Euglena and other protists
subtopics.concept: Euglena: flagellum at the anterior end attached at the base of the flask-shaped reservoir; contractile vacuole near the reservoir; gullet; numerous chloroplasts; light-sensitive eyespot (stigma); no cell wall but a flexible pellicle; nucleus. It reproduces by binary fission and forms cysts in bad conditions.

topics.title: Animal kingdom
topics.concept: Animals are classified into invertebrate phyla (cnidarians, flatworms, roundworms, annelids, arthropods, molluscs, echinoderms) and vertebrate classes (fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals).

subtopics.title: Invertebrates and vertebrates
subtopics.concept: Flatworms are acoelomate, roundworms (nematodes) pseudocoelomate, annelids and higher animals coelomate. Insects show metamorphosis: incomplete (egg → nymph → adult, grasshopper) or complete (egg → larva → pupa → adult, butterfly, housefly). Chondrichthyes (sharks, rays) have a cartilage skeleton, true jaws, two pairs of fins and a two-chambered heart.

topics.title: Biomolecules and nutrition
topics.unit: G9 Unit 3; G10 Unit 1 – Food and Digestion
topics.concept: Carbohydrates, lipids, proteins and nucleic acids are the biomolecules (building blocks) of cells. The six nutrients are carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, vitamins, minerals and water.

subtopics.title: Carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, nucleic acids
subtopics.concept: Saturated fats (animal fats, solid at room temperature) have more hydrogen atoms than unsaturated fats (plant oils, liquid).

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 3 – Metabolic Processes and Energy Transfers in Living Organisms
Unit 3 – Metabolic Processes and Energy Transfers in Living Organisms

subtopics.title: Nutrients and deficiency diseases
subtopics.concept: Lack of protein → kwashiorkor; lack of energy foods → marasmus; lack of vitamin D → rickets. Fats need bile for emulsification before digestion.

Unit 3 – Metabolic Processes and Energy Transfers in Living Organisms

topics.title: Human digestive system
topics.concept: Digestion is mechanical and chemical. Teeth, saliva, stomach, liver/bile, pancreas and small intestine enzymes break food down; nutrients are absorbed in the small intestine.

subtopics.title: Teeth, swallowing, enzymes and bile
subtopics.concept: Dental formula = teeth on one side of upper/lower jaw; total = sum × 2 (dog i 3/3 c 1/1 pm 4/4 m 2/3 = 42; human 32). During swallowing the soft palate closes the nasal cavity and the epiglottis closes the trachea. Sucrase (invertase) digests sucrose → glucose + fructose. Bile from the liver is stored in the gall bladder and emulsifies fats.

topics.title: Circulatory, lymphatic and immune systems
topics.concept: The heart pumps blood in a closed double circulation; lymph returns tissue fluid in a one-way system; the immune system defends the body by active and passive immunity.

subtopics.title: Heart and blood vessels
subtopics.concept: The human heart has two atria and two ventricles. AV valves (tricuspid, bicuspid) close at the start of ventricular contraction ('lub'); semilunar valves close afterwards ('dub'). Arteries carry blood away from the heart under high pressure; veins have valves and are helped by skeletal-muscle contraction.

textbook_refs.section: 3.1.2 Lymphatic Vessels – skeletal muscle action moves lymph
2.1.1 The Human Heart – heart valves and cardiac cycle

subtopics.title: Blood groups and the Rh factor
subtopics.concept: An Rh-negative person given Rh-positive blood makes anti-Rh antibodies; a second Rh-positive transfusion causes agglutination. Similar sensitisation causes Rh disease in a second Rh-positive pregnancy.

textbook_refs.section: 2.5 Blood Types – the Rh blood group

subtopics.title: Lymph, lymph vessels and lymph nodes
subtopics.concept: The lymphatic system is one-way (tissues → veins) with no pump; lymph is moved by skeletal muscles, breathing and smooth muscle. Lymph nodes are bean-shaped organs containing many leukocytes.

textbook_refs.section: 3.2 Comparison between the Lymphatic System and the Circulatory System

subtopics.title: Active and passive immunity
subtopics.concept: Active immunity: own antibodies (natural after infection, artificial after vaccination). Passive immunity: ready-made antibodies (natural – mother to baby via placenta/milk; artificial – serum or anti-venom injection); immediate but short-lived.

topics.title: Respiratory system
topics.concept: Air passes nose → pharynx → larynx → trachea → bronchi → lungs. Breathing is driven by the diaphragm and intercostal muscles.

subtopics.title: Respiratory organs and breathing mechanism
subtopics.concept: The larynx (voice box) is an airway and produces sound: vocal cords vibrate as exhaled air passes. Inhalation: diaphragm contracts (pulls down), ribs move up and out, lungs expand. Exhalation: diaphragm relaxes to its dome shape.

topics.title: Excretion, sense organs and nervous system
topics.concept: Skin, lungs, liver and kidneys excrete wastes. Receptors detect stimuli; the brain and spinal cord integrate them and reflexes give fast automatic responses.

subtopics.title: Excretory organs and kidney failure
subtopics.concept: Skin excretes sweat (water, salts, urea), lungs CO₂ and water, liver bile pigments and urea formation, kidneys urine. Kidney failure is treated with an artificial kidney (dialysis, short-term) or kidney transplant (long-term).

textbook_refs.section: 5.4 The Control of Body Temperature – skin
4 The Immune System – skin as barrier

subtopics.title: External and internal receptors; hearing defects
subtopics.concept: Internal receptors detect muscle length and tension, limb position, pain, blood composition, volume and pressure, body temperature. Deafness: calcified/pierced eardrum, excessive noise, blows on the cheek, pointed objects in the canal, fused ossicles.

subtopics.title: Brain, impulses and reflexes
subtopics.concept: Cerebral lobes: frontal (voluntary movement), parietal (sensation), temporal (hearing, smell, memory), occipital (vision). Hypothalamus: temperature, blood pressure, water balance, appetite, emotions, pituitary control. Threshold = minimum stimulus that starts an impulse. A reflex is an automatic, involuntary response via a reflex arc through the spinal cord.

textbook_refs.section: 8.2.1 The Central Nervous System – the cerebrum

topics.title: Endocrine, reproductive, skeletal and muscular systems
topics.concept: Hormones are chemical messengers of endocrine glands. The reproductive system produces gametes and supports pregnancy. Bones and muscles support and move the body.

subtopics.title: Endocrine glands and hormones
subtopics.concept: Hormones are proteins, steroids or amino-acid derivatives. Pituitary: GH, TSH, ACTH, prolactin (milk production), FSH, LH; posterior lobe releases ADH (water balance) and oxytocin (uterine contraction, milk release). Pancreas: beta cells → insulin, alpha cells → glucagon.

subtopics.title: Homeostasis: blood glucose and body temperature
subtopics.concept: Insulin lowers and glucagon raises blood glucose. The skin regulates temperature by sweating and changes in blood flow.

textbook_refs.section: 5.4 The Control of Body Temperature – skin
4 The Immune System – skin as barrier

subtopics.title: Human reproduction and pregnancy
subtopics.concept: Secondary sexual characteristics in both sexes: growth spurt, pubic and armpit hair; males: deeper voice, facial hair. Seminal vesicle: alkaline fluid with prostaglandins; Cowper's gland: lubricating mucus. Progesterone maintains the uterine lining. Umbilical vein carries food and O₂ to the fetus; umbilical arteries carry wastes away.

subtopics.title: Bone structure; axial and appendicular skeleton
subtopics.concept: Bone layers: periosteum (smooth double-layered covering), compact bone, spongy bone. Axial skeleton: skull, vertebral column, sternum, ribs; appendicular: limbs and girdles.

subtopics.title: Skeletal, smooth and cardiac muscles
subtopics.concept: Smooth muscle lines hollow organs, blood vessels, eyes, glands and skin; cardiac muscle is found only in the heart.

topics.title: Plant systems
topics.concept: Seeds germinate (radicle first), growth is controlled by hormones such as auxin (IAA), leaves photosynthesise in the mesophyll, and flowers reproduce by double fertilization.

subtopics.title: Germination and plant hormones
subtopics.concept: The radicle emerges first, then the plumule. IAA is the natural auxin made in the shoot apical meristem; NAA and 2,4-D are synthetic auxins; cytokinins and ABA are other hormone classes.

subtopics.title: Leaf structure
subtopics.concept: Upper and lower epidermis are separated by the mesophyll (palisade + spongy layers); the waxy cuticle covers the epidermis.

subtopics.title: Double fertilization
subtopics.concept: One male nucleus fuses with the egg (zygote); the second fuses with the two polar nuclei to form the endosperm – double fertilization, found only in flowering plants.

topics.title: Nucleic acids, cell division and genetics
topics.concept: DNA is transcribed into mRNA; mitosis makes identical body cells and meiosis makes haploid gametes; Mendel's laws explain inheritance; sex-linked genes lie on the sex chromosomes.

subtopics.title: DNA, RNA and transcription
subtopics.concept: RNA has uracil instead of thymine. Transcription pairs DNA A→U, T→A, G→C, C→G (ATGCA → UACGU).

subtopics.title: Mitosis and meiosis
subtopics.concept: Mitosis: prophase (chromosomes shorten and thicken), metaphase, anaphase, telophase. Meiosis produces haploid (monoploid) gametes.

subtopics.title: Mendelian genetics and test crosses
subtopics.concept: Mendel chose peas: quick maturity, controllable pollination, fertile seeds after crossing, contrasting characters. A test cross with the homozygous recessive shows whether a dominant individual is homozygous or heterozygous; Ff × ff gives 1 : 1.

subtopics.title: Sex-linked characters
subtopics.concept: Sex-linked genes are on sex chromosomes, mostly X. X-linked recessive traits (colour blindness, haemophilia) affect mostly males; a colour-blind daughter needs a colour-blind father and a carrier or colour-blind mother.

topics.title: Evolution, adaptation and ecology
topics.concept: Evolution is gradual change in populations over time, supported by fossils, comparative anatomy, embryology, biochemistry and geographical distribution. Organisms are adapted to their environments; energy flows through food chains and webs within biomes.

subtopics.title: Theories and evidence of evolution
subtopics.concept: Evolution changes populations, not individuals. Homologous organs indicate a common ancestor; greater similarity means closer relationship.

subtopics.title: Adaptations of plants and animals
subtopics.concept: Cold: fur, fat, higher metabolism, shivering, hibernation, small ears. Heat: large ears, no fat layer (camel), evaporative cooling. Salt: mangroves. Dry: cactus.

subtopics.title: Food chains and food webs
subtopics.concept: A food chain is a single linear sequence of energy flow; a food web is many interconnected food chains, more complex and more stable.

textbook_refs.section: 3.3 Food Relationships – food chains and food webs

subtopics.title: Biomes of the world
subtopics.concept: Tropical rain forests (equatorial belt, warm and wet all year) harbour more species than any other terrestrial biome; tundra and taiga are cold with low diversity.

textbook_refs.section: 3.5 Biomes of the World – tropical rain forest
